name: Neuroferritinopathy
aliases: Neurodegeneration with Brain Iron Accumulation Type 2

ethnicAssociations: Predominantly reported in individuals of European descent

criteria.description: Presence of progressive movement disorders including chorea, dystonia, or parkinsonism
MRI evidence of iron accumulation in basal ganglia and other brain regions
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the FTL1 gene
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Exclusion of other neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA) disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive movement disorder, MRI evidence of brain iron accumulation, and pathogenic FTL1 gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis.

common.symptomName: Abnormality of blood and blood-forming tissues

laboratory: Elevated serum ferritin levels may be present but not consistent
imaging: MRI showing hypointense signals in basal ganglia on T2-weighted and susceptibility-weighted imaging
Iron deposition in globus pallidus, putamen, and caudate nucleus
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in the FTL1 gene (ferritin light chain gene)

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic 'eye of the tiger' sign on MRI
Systemic iron overload including diabetes and retinal degeneration
GAA trinucleotide repeat expansions in FXN gene

redFlags: Early cognitive decline in a young adult
Family history of similar neurodegenerative symptoms
references: Hogarth P. Neuroferritinopathy: pathogenesis, presentation and management. J Mov Disord. 2015;8(1):1-9.
Chinnery PF, et al. Neuroferritinopathy: a new autosomal dominant disease associated with abnormal ferritin storage in the brain. Nat Genet. 2003;33(4): 381-385.
